thread:
maya: Heads-up — seeing a noisy node in us-west1-az-b. ECC counter spiked, Xid bursts, temp jitter. Auto-signal fired but node wasn't drained.
liam: which node id?
maya: node-azb-gpu-12345. logs: http://logs.internal/azb/12345 (redacted)
ops-bot: ALERT: gpu_health.alert triggered for node-azb-gpu-12345 — metrics: ecc_delta=27, xid_rate=142/m, temp_sigma=5.2. Debounce window: 300s.
sophia: hmm we recently increased debounce to 5m. Maybe the burst fell under threshold after the first sample and the autopilot didn't re-evaluate.
andre: can we make drain decision depend on correlated signals (ecc + xid + pci_err_rate) instead of single-metric threshold?
rene: agreed. Also propose soft-preempt path: soft-cordon -> move running Slurm job to drain queue -> if jobs don't migrate within T, force-evict. Keeps pods scheduled but avoids hard kills.
liam: +1. runbook sketch:
```
# soft-preempt sequence
kubectl label node node-azb-gpu-12345 redwood/autodrain=preempting
kubectl cordon node-azb-gpu-12345
# for Slurm nodes: set state DRAIN via scontrol
scontrol update NodeName=node-azb-gpu-12345 State=DRAIN Reason="gpu_health_autopreempt"
# wait policy: 10m soft window, then force evict
kubectl drain node-azb-gpu-12345 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 || true
```
maya: That looks good. We should also attach a safety window so we don't oscillate (e.g., no re-cordon for 30m after a soft-preempt).
sophia: Also add rate-limiting per-region — don't pull >5% of GPUs in a AZ for reprovision at once.
andre: Cost note: reprovisioning/reimage churn has a small cost (~$0.15/node for short reprovision), but avoided OOMs are worth it. I'll add metric for reprovision_count in billing dashboard.
rene: For signal correlation, draft alert rule idea:
```
expr = (increase(gpu_ecc_errors[5m]) > 10 and increase(gpu_xid_errors[5m]) > 100) or (gpu_temp_jitter > 4 and increase(pcie_errs[5m]) > 5)
actions: emit `gpu_health.alert` with severity=medium and runbook=soft-preempt.
```
liam: Can we have a preview mode on staging that simulates the full sequence (cordon + slurm drain + node reprovision) without actually evicting? Would help validate corner cases.
maya: yes — we have `evac-bot --dry-run` support. ops-bot, can you trigger a dry run on node-azb-gpu-12345?
ops-bot: evactool invoked: `evac-bot --dry-run --node node-azb-gpu-12345 --reason gpu_health_alert` — simulation started.
evac-bot: DRY-RUN: would cordon node, set Slurm DRAIN, mark reprovision candidate. No live evictions performed. Estimated impacted jobs: 2 (interactive), 1 (batch).
andre: simulation output looks sane. Two interactive jobs flagged; they have preemptible labels so will migrate.
maya: Let's run a real soft-preempt after a 10m observation window if signals persist. I'll bump the debounce to 120s for this rule.
liam: filing a short follow-up doc in /wiki/infrastructure/autodrain-preempt with the sequence + safety controls. I'll own the postmortem if this escalates.
sophia: can we also add a metric to track how often autopreempt is blocked by debounce? want visibility.
rene: I'll add reprovision_count, autopreempt_blocked_count and region_quarantine_count to the console.
maya: Thanks team. Running trial in us-west1-az-b with conservative limits. Will update in 15m. :thumbsup:
